reasons.reproducibility: Bench Microcystis with chlorine, ozone, KMnO4, CuSO4 and H2O2 needs an ozone generator and flow cytometry.
reasons.effectiveness: Oxidants compromised membranes (chlorine >=88% in 1 min, ozone 90% in 5 min), but cell densities fell only ~22% (Cu) and ~15% (KMnO4), not at all with ozone or H2O2, and cells recovered after day 3.
reasons.cost: Ozone generator and cell-integrity assays about $150-500.
reasons.environment: All oxidants lyse membranes and release toxins; CuSO4 arm adds metal.

reasons.reproducibility: Needs an ozone generator, flow cytometry and GC analysis of chlorinated by-products.
reasons.effectiveness: Preozonation at 0.4-2.0 mg/L left <=1% intact cells and raised coagulation removal from 56.7% to 80.2%, but tests were duplicates only and permanganate kept >97% of cells alive.
reasons.environment: Dramatically increased chlorinated disinfection by-products; releases intracellular matter.

reasons.reproducibility: 2,000 L mesocosms plus a lake-embayment field trial with nanobubble ozone gear.
reasons.effectiveness: Triplicate 2,000 L mesocosms cut chl a 98-99% at 7-15 mg O3/L, but on water diluted 60%; two 4-week lake trials showed no effect (within +/-10% of inlet).
reasons.cost: Nanobubble ozone system and field trials well over $5,000.
reasons.time: 4-week field trials; mesocosm effect faster, scored 1-3 weeks.
reasons.environment: Oxidized DOC; minimal reach; no reported harm but uncertain.

reasons.reproducibility: Replicated mesocosms with nanobubble ozone and label-rate algaecides.
reasons.effectiveness: Non-target study on a green-algae-dominated community; phytoplankton fell similarly in all treatments, so no bloom-control effect is shown.
reasons.environment: Zooplankton grew +120% in controls but only +10% under high-dose ozone (Bosmina reduced), versus -80% copper and -90% peroxide.

reasons.reproducibility: Typical reviewed experiment is UV-C on a bench culture, doable with a sponsor's UV lamp.
reasons.effectiveness: UV-C suppresses growth with dose (e.g. 80% Chattonella kill in 40 s from a boat), but species sensitivity varies and photoreactivation/dark repair cause regrowth; mostly static lab tests.
reasons.time: UV effect seen within hours to days.
reasons.environment: No chemical residue; non-target effects on other plankton not assessed.

reasons.reproducibility: Petri-dish UV-C exposure of a Microcystis culture with a germicidal lamp for 30 s-2 min is bench work, needing a sponsor for UV safety.
reasons.effectiveness: All doses held cells below 25% of control by day 3 in triplicate; 150 mW s/cm2 killed all cells by day 7 while 37-75 stopped division (controls grew ~20x).
reasons.cost: UV lamp, radiometer and culture about $150-500.
reasons.time: Density fell below 25% of control by day 3.
reasons.environment: No chemical added; micromolar H2O2 formed; residual effect from treated exudates.

reasons.reproducibility: Chlorinating Microcystis suspensions with microcystin analysis needs ELISA/LC-MS.
reasons.effectiveness: Low chlorine lysed cells (63% K+ release) but released toxin faster than it degraded.
reasons.cost: Chlorine is cheap but microcystin analysis is $150-500.
reasons.environment: Low chlorine raised dissolved microcystin; by-product precursors released.

reasons.reproducibility: Microelectrolysis with DSA, Pt and BDD anodes is specialist electrochemistry.
reasons.effectiveness: Electrolysed seawater (hypochlorite ~5.8 mg/L) removed 81.7 +/- 2.3% (DSA) of Heterosigma, 64-70% with Pt/BDD, measured by fluorescence.
reasons.cost: Pt and BDD anodes plus a high-current supply push it to $500-5,000.
reasons.environment: Effectively electro-chlorination; hypochlorite can rupture cells and release toxin, and no ecological tests were done.

reasons.reproducibility: Synthesizing g-C3N4/TiO2 films needs a materials lab.
reasons.effectiveness: 64% net inactivation of K. mikimotoi in 60 min vs dark and light-only controls (light-only fluorescence recovered).
reasons.environment: Film is immobilised and reusable and cytotoxicity fell, but ~71% of intracellular organic matter was released.

reasons.reproducibility: 30 mL bottles with TiO2-coated glass beads under a 365 nm LED panel and cell counts are a bench protocol a sponsor can support.
reasons.effectiveness: In triplicate, cells fell 35% from the start while both controls grew +213-226%, leaving treated density ~70% below controls; decline began only after 48 h.
reasons.environment: Immobilised catalyst is retrievable, and total microcystins fell 74% with released toxin fully destroyed.

reasons.reproducibility: Ozonation of toxic Cochlodinium in seawater needs an ozone generator and cultures.
reasons.effectiveness: Ozone >1 mg/L removed all viable C. polykrikoides within 300 s (5 mg/L in 100 s), but efficacy fell with cell density, humics, pH and temperature and replication is not stated.
reasons.environment: Ozonated seawater formed bromate at 278 ug/L at 5 mg/L ozone (WHO guideline 10 ug/L), negligible below 1 mg/L.

reasons.reproducibility: Canal-scale ozone system processing 300 gal/min; industrial gear.
reasons.effectiveness: No cell or toxin numbers published; press says it worked 'sort of'.
reasons.environment: Not reported beyond scale concerns; ozone by-products in seawater uncertain.
